primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4617163/ | Methods, cluster ascertainment and discussion
assessment: This regional clinical study identified 92 patients with progressive supranuclear palsy and investigated geographic concentration and industrial metal contamination. Its exposure assessment and clinical data do not supply a fresh-thyme or olfactory comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7262311/ | Olfactory training review, reference 32 and Appendix 1
assessment: The early postviral smell primer gives thyme as one of four sniffed odors in the middle training block and cites Altundag's postinfectious study. It supplies a multi-odor olfactory treatment lead without isolating thyme, ingestion or Parkinson disease.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11925478/ | Abstract 114, Aromatic Plants and Parkinson’s Disease, reference 1
assessment: The review's sole human trial is the already assessed marjoram tea trial PMID 34455218. The reported benefit concerns nonmotor summary scores. This is a secondary route to that cohort and supplies no separate dried-leaf walking-slowness estimate.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10854369/ | Abstracts 142–143, especially quercetin and zinc-oxide toxicity
assessment: Abstract 143 uses corn oil as one mouse control in a quercetin and zinc-oxide experiment measuring hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal toxicity. The adjacent Parkinson exercise abstract measures motor/cognitive outcomes after aerobic exercise, without a corn-oil attention comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6157254/ | Vegetable acceptance educational intervention Methods, bell-pepper list
assessment: The bell pepper is one of several lunch vegetables in a school nutrition session. The reward and outcomes concern children's vegetable consumption and acceptance, without a grilled preparation or a Parkinson walking-speed test.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4056556/ | Methods, supplement prevalence table and adverse-effects table
assessment: The hospice guide reviews how to take a supplement history. Flaxseed appears in prevalence tables, and insomnia appears among cautions for other herbs or supplements. No cold-pressed flaxseed oil insomnia study is reported.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4429500/ | J Andrews and AD Fotino, Mother Nature to the Rescue?, ID 1926245
assessment: The case describes flaxseed oil taken during repeated episodes of a rash and separately lists drowsiness as an antihistamine adverse effect. Its clinical endpoint is urticaria and it gives no cold-pressed flaxseed oil or insomnia comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11231130/ | Author Cinnamon Etta presentation and the separate haloperidol case
assessment: Cinnamon Etta is a named author. Masked facies appears in a distinct clinical case involving extrapyramidal signs after haloperidol. These give no ground cinnamon intervention or Parkinson facial-expression outcome.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4070603/ | Urban-population GERD and dietary questionnaire; P152 normal endoscopy
assessment: One abstract lists potatoes among foods more frequently reported by urban participants with GERD. P152 separately reviews gastroscopy investigations in dysphagia. The protocols do not connect an identified baked potato exposure to a Parkinson swallowing outcome.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4212306/ | Radiolabeled mashed potato gastric-emptying test and postprandial FMD crossover
assessment: The abstracts use labeled mashed potato for gastric emptying or compare guar addition and meal pacing for postprandial flow-mediated dilation. Malignant dysphagia and stenting are separate, including poster P0121. They do not report a baked potato swallowing comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4669991/ | P0444 low-FODMAP colonic MRI and separate stricture stenting reports
assessment: P0444 mentions potato as possible fermentable substrate in an explanation of low-FODMAP colonic volume findings. The adjacent clinical dysphagia protocols concern structural disease and stents. These are different endpoints and presentations.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5391000/ | High-fat meal gastric-accommodation experiment and separate Parkinson PEJ report
assessment: The reflux study administers meatloaf, mashed potato and apple sauce as a mixed meal to reflux/dyspepsia patients and healthy controls. The separate Parkinson report concerns a jejunal route for levodopa–carbidopa. Neither gives baked potato swallowing severity.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6265811/ | P20-020 dietary fat and Parkinson diagnosis; P20-066 potato and mortality
assessment: The Swedish cohort follows dietary fat and Parkinson incidence. The separately numbered NIH-AARP study pools several potato preparations for mortality analyses. Neither studies swallowing difficulty from baked potato in Parkinson disease.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7161410/ | Chapter sections on atypical interstitial pneumonia and clinical signs in large animals
assessment: The veterinary chapter describes mold-damaged sweet potatoes as a proposed cause of bovine pulmonary injury. Dysphagia refers to signs of other large-animal disorders such as pharyngeal nerve disease, without a baked potato patient comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7162159/ | Fungal culture posters and separate dysphagia in parasitic infection case
assessment: Potato dextrose agar is a microbial culture substrate in separate laboratory posters. Dysphagia is described as an early symptom in a parasitic infection case. Neither is a potato exposure in Parkinson disease.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7170211/ | Specific Problem Areas, oral mucositis Box 3.5 and food guidance
assessment: The chapter lists rough foods such as crisps or potato chips in guidance for cancer-treatment oral mucositis and reports a clinical grading scheme based on ulcers and pain. It supplies no baked potato clinical contrast in Parkinson disease.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9045588/ | Infrared tray drying, pharmacology and methotrexate mucocutaneous case
assessment: The tray-drying presentation uses potato among product samples for drying-time comparisons. Dysphagia is a separate case symptom after methotrexate toxicity; Parkinson and plant extracts appear in other pharmacology presentations.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9771678/ | Glossary entry tuber
assessment: The glossary uses potato as an example of a plant storage structure under tuber. The archival terminology reference supplies no treated population or food swallowing outcome.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1490295/ | Abstract 134053, Mistaking Apples for Oranges
assessment: A patient with an acute ischemic stroke used the word potato when naming corn-on-the-cob. The report concerns aphasic object naming and patent foramen ovale rather than a potato bolus or Parkinson dysphagia.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7019188/ | T1P158 randomized potato-fiber crossover
assessment: The placebo-controlled crossover tests potato-fiber formulations incorporated into buns in healthy men and measures appetite and fecal fat excretion. Neither the form nor the outcome matches a baked potato swallowing response in Parkinson disease.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7103899/ | Presentation 108, Role of hydrogen breath test in functional dyspepsia
assessment: The protocol asks patients to avoid potato and other foods ahead of a fasting hydrogen breath test, then administers glucose. The outcome is gastrointestinal bacterial overgrowth, without a potato swallow challenge.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8454868/ | Disaccharidase-activity poster and separate Parkinson PEG-J and constipation posters
assessment: The carbohydrate-disaccharidase study records intestinal symptoms in relation to potato-starch foods. Separate Parkinson posters concern PEG-J delivery or chronic constipation rather than potato boluses and swallowing.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8260309/ | Antimicrobial bioactivity discussion and crop pathology references
assessment: Potato appears in a discussion of bacterial causes of crop brown rot and soft rot that are inhibited by Peganum preparations. These are plant pathology or laboratory endpoints rather than consumption or clinical swallowing.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11520510/ | Characteristics of included Parkinson trials and prescribed diet table
assessment: Parkinson dysphagia appears in one constipation trial's eligibility, and fries or potato chips occur in a separate diet list. The systematic review assesses constipation and fecal incontinence interventions, without a baked potato swallowing effect.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11469791/ | Table of phytate content, seed-only eggplant row, and CKD discussion
assessment: The table reports phytate content for eggplant seed and gives no cooked serving estimate. The review evaluates mineral and kidney outcomes rather than olfactory change from eating baked eggplant.
